observation.visible_scene: A low-angle view of a shallow forest stream tumbling over dark, wet rocks. Lush green foliage fills the upper and left frame, a thick bare tree branch arches across the top from the right, and a dark mossy rock/earth wall bounds the right side. In the background the channel opens into a bright, fog-filled gap where diffuse light glows through the mist.
visible_changes: The white frothy rapids in the middle of the stream continuously churn, with foam patches changing shape and brightening/dimming from frame to frame as water moves toward the foreground.
The pale streak of aerated water in the lower-left foreground shifts and reforms slightly across the sequence, consistent with steady downstream flow.
The central turbulent water texture is in constant motion, indicating an ongoing flow rather than a start or stop.
The arching branch, the lining rocks, the surrounding leaves, and the right-side dark wall keep the same screen positions throughout, so the camera is essentially fixed.
The background mist and glow remain largely steady, with only subtle density variation.
outside_clip_unknowns: The upstream source and downstream continuation of the stream.
What produces the background light and mist (sun angle, waterfall, etc.).
Any wind or current that might affect the foliage.
Events before t=0 and after t=2.67s.
uncertain_details: Whether there is any very slight camera drift versus a perfectly locked-off shot.
Whether individual leaves sway subtly; motion is dominated by the water.
Exact trajectories of single foam patches, which are hard to track frame to frame.
